tasks.short: Scan journal alerts and working papers, read the important ones, discuss with colleagues in seminars, serve in professional associations, choose and register for conferences, and attend them.

steps.what: Business teacher scans journal alerts and new working papers

loop.input: The week's journal alerts and working paper abstracts on the teacher's topics.
loop.output: A weekly digest grouping papers by topic, each line linked to its paper.
loop.check: Code drops any line whose link does not resolve by DOI or repository identifier; the teacher picks what to read.
loop.stop: One digest per week; papers that cannot be grouped are listed by title.
loop.why_not_simpler: A keyword filter lists titles but cannot say what each paper adds.

steps.what: Business teacher keeps abreast of developments by reading current literature
Business teacher talks with colleagues in research seminars
Business teacher participates in professional organizations
Business teacher chooses which conferences to attend
Business teacher registers for the chosen conferences
Business teacher participates in professional conferences

tasks.design: Journal alerts and working paper feeds go into one weekly digest: a bounded step groups papers by topic with a line on what each adds, and code drops any line whose link does not resolve. The teacher reads the papers that matter in full. Seminars, association work and conferences stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alerts piled up in the inbox and were scanned title by title.
tasks.enabler_now: Research tools summarise topics and point to papers.
tasks.still_hard: A summary can miss why a paper matters for one's own work.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in a seminar corridor what a paper does not say.
tasks.altitude: The teacher reads selected papers instead of scanning every alert.

reach.learn: Whether a shared digest helps the group.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and points to foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: from journal alerts to conference insights; own research is outside.
Input contract: alerts from the library's databases and working paper feeds; fallback is scanning the inbox.
Reading, seminars, association work and conferences do not change.
Conference fees are approved as today.
research_questions: Does the teacher read more relevant papers?

already_counted.description: Business teacher reads the weekly digest.

approvals.approved_version: The conferences as chosen by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a narrow field with few alerts; high: a broad field with many working papers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review course evaluations and results, discuss revisions with the programme committee, revise course content and the manual, update exercises and cases, check the course with the coordinator, and publish it.

steps.what: Business teacher evaluates the course from student evaluations and results
Business teacher discusses revisions with the programme committee and colleagues
Business teacher revises course content and the course manual

loop.input: The agreed revisions, the catalogue's learning outcomes and the current manual.
loop.output: Draft revised sections of the course manual.
loop.check: Code checks every learning outcome is covered by at least one week and one assessment; the teacher edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when coverage passes and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: Manual sections explain the course in prose; a coverage table alone does not.

steps.what: Business teacher revises exercises and cases with new figures
Business teacher checks the revised course with the programme coordinator
Business teacher uploads the revised course materials

tasks.design: A course dashboard ({BI}) joins student evaluation scores, pass rates and item analysis, so the teacher reads them in one place. A bounded step drafts revised manual sections from the agreed changes; code checks every learning outcome is covered, and the teacher edits. Accounting and finance exercises get new number variants from a generator whose answer keys are computed by code. Once the coordinator has agreed, the course is published in the learning environment ({LMS}). Deciding revisions with the committee stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evaluation data sat in separate files and manuals and exercises were reworked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards join course data; exercise generators compute answer keys; language models draft text.
tasks.still_hard: Good revisions come from what happened in the classroom.
tasks.human_edge: Replacing a dull case with one from a local company students know.
tasks.altitude: The teacher decides revisions and edits drafts instead of reworking materials by hand.

evidence.claim: EduGenAI is a chat platform for Dutch education in pilot at Utrecht University, which forbids automated grading on it.
Revising course manuals is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from course results to the course published; programme-level changes are outside.
Input contract: evaluations and results from the institution's systems; learning outcomes from the catalogue; fallback is reworking by hand.
No student names go into the drafting step.
research_questions: Do pass rates change after revisions?

already_counted.description: Business teacher edits and approves drafted manual sections.

incremental.description: Business teacher sets up exercise templates for the generator.

approvals.approved_version: The course as checked with the programme coordinator in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: courses with few numeric exercises; high: accounting and finance courses with many exercises.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record tutorial attendance, have students sign in, combine quiz, assignment and exam grades, check final grades, register them, answer grade questions, and keep exam archives.

steps.what: Business teacher maintains student attendance records for tutorials
Students sign the tutorial attendance list
Business teacher combines quiz, assignment and exam grades in a spreadsheet
Business teacher checks final grades and borderline cases as examiner
Business teacher types the grades into the student administration system
Business teacher answers grade questions and inspection requests by e-mail
Business teacher keeps exam archives for the examination board

tasks.design: Students check in to tutorials by scanning a code in the learning environment ({LMS}). Its gradebook computes the weighted final grade by the course's rules, and students see their grade breakdown in the portal, which cuts routine questions. Once the teacher has checked final grades and borderline cases as examiner, grades pass to student administration ({OTHER}) without retyping. Exams are archived digitally with retention dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance lists, grade spreadsheets and typed grades in two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments compute weighted grades and pass them to student administration.
tasks.still_hard: Borderline cases and exceptions need the examiner's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a disappointing grade so the student knows what to do next.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks grades and handles exceptions instead of computing and typing.

reach.learn: Whether archives are complete when asked.

evidence.claim: At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, a double entry.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from the tutorial list to the exam archive; exam board decisions are outside.
Input contract: class lists from student administration; grading rules set by the examiner; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Students scan a code in about the time signing took, and look up their grade breakdown in the portal; priced as customer time.
Checking final grades stays with the examiner.
research_questions: Do grade questions by e-mail fall?

incremental.description: Business teacher sets grading rules in the gradebook each term.
Students scan the tutorial code and read their grade breakdown.

approvals.approved_version: The final grades as checked by the examiner in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small courses with few graded parts; high: large courses with many quizzes and questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review literature, collect company and market data, analyze it, write the paper, format the manuscript, check it with co-authors, submit it, and respond to reviewers.

steps.what: Business teacher reviews the literature for the research question
Business teacher collects company and market data from databases
Business teacher conducts research by analyzing the data
Business teacher writes the paper to publish findings in professional journals
Business teacher formats the manuscript and references to the journal's style
Business teacher checks the final manuscript with co-authors
Business teacher submits the manuscript through the journal's portal
Business teacher responds to reviewers and revises the paper

tasks.design: Research tools summarise topics and point to the key papers, so the literature review starts from a map rather than a blank search. Company and market data are pulled from licensed databases by saved, scripted queries that can be rerun. A reference manager formats citations to each journal's style. Analysis, writing, checking with co-authors, submitting and answering reviewers stay with the teacher; no model writes the findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searches and data downloads were redone by hand for each project.
tasks.enabler_now: Research tools map literature; databases allow scripted downloads; reference managers format citations.
tasks.still_hard: Original ideas and careful analysis cannot be sped up.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the question in company data that nobody has asked.

reach.learn: Whether scripted downloads make work reproducible.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and points to foundational papers.
Reference managers format citations to journal styles.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the revision submitted; the publisher's editing is outside.
Input contract: database licences from the library; fallback is manual searching and downloads.
Analysis, writing and reviewing do not change.
Journals accept reference styles from reference managers.
research_questions: Does time from idea to submission fall?

incremental.description: Business teacher maintains the saved data queries.

approvals.approved_version: The paper as checked with co-authors in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: theory papers with little data; high: empirical papers with large data pulls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The business teacher keeps reading, deciding course changes, judging grades and doing original research; scanning alerts, reworking exercises, combining grades and redoing data pulls shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time on research and students.
